title: Nvidia Packs Seven Vera Rubin Racks Into Truck-Shipped DSX Pod
excerpt: The container-sized DSX Pod arrives with cabling and liquid cooling pre-installed, cutting AI data centre deployment at a prepared site from six months to 14 days, with partner deliveries due in early 2027.
body:
• Nvidia's DSX Pod packs seven Vera Rubin NVL72 racks — 504 Rubin GPUs and 252 Vera CPUs — into a container about 28,000 kilograms that can travel by truck on normal roads.
  • All cabling, networking, rack-level power and liquid cooling are installed and validated in the factory, cutting deployment at a prepared site from six months to as little as 14 days.
  • Partners including Dell Technologies, HPE, Foxconn, Lenovo and Vertiv will deliver the pods worldwide in early 2027; Nvidia disclosed no price, while analysts put a single Vera Rubin rack at more than $7 million.
  • For operators racing to add AI capacity, the gain is time to first token: a factory-tested pod can start serving production workloads weeks after arrival instead of months into an on-site build.

Nvidia on Wednesday introduced the DSX Pod at GTC Berlin, a reference design that puts seven of its Vera Rubin AI racks into a modular container roughly the size of a standard shipping container. The company said the pod weighs about 28,000 kilograms, nearly 62,000 pounds, is designed to be shipped on a truck on normal roads, and arrives with its cabling and liquid cooling already assembled at the factory, according to CNBC reporting carried in other outlets and Nvidia's own announcement.

The design extends Nvidia's move from single GPUs to servers, then to entire racks, and now to a containerised block with racks already integrated.

"The only thing that has to happen when it gets to the site is it's placed in its location, connected to the rest of the other containers, and validated through final burning and testing."

— Ian Buck, Vice President of Hyperscale Computing, Nvidia

What Is Inside the Pod

Each pod holds seven Vera Rubin NVL72 racks. Each rack pairs 72 Rubin GPUs with 36 Vera CPUs, putting 504 GPUs and 252 CPUs inside a single pod, according to The Register. Partners complete rack-to-rack cabling, wiring, piping and functional validation before shipment, Nvidia said in its DSX Pod announcement.

In a traditional build, that integration happens on site with specialised labour and logistics. Nvidia said moving it into the factory reduces exposure to component delays and error-prone on-site work, and lets site preparation proceed in parallel.

The 14-day claim carries a condition: it applies at a prepared site. The units arrive ready to connect out of the box to power, cooling, networking and other supporting infrastructure that must already be in place. The pod does not eliminate site work; it removes the rack integration from the site's critical path.

Why Speed Is the Selling Point

Nvidia frames deployment speed as revenue speed. The company measures a new factory by time to first token, when it begins running models to serve production workloads. A site that starts serving tokens in 14 days rather than six months can begin earning from the same hardware far sooner.

"An AI factory creates value when it starts producing tokens — not when construction is complete."

— Jensen Huang, Founder and CEO, Nvidia

Huang added that with DSX Pod, Nvidia is bringing "factory-built precision and speed to AI infrastructure construction — reducing deployment time from months to weeks so customers can scale capacity and bring revenue-generating production online faster." Nvidia said the pod is intended for customers worldwide and could help address deployment challenges faced by European customers.

The economics behind the push are rising. Nvidia did not announce a price for the pod, but analysts say a single Vera Rubin rack can cost more than $7 million. Speaking recently on a podcast, Huang said what Nvidia offers into one gigawatt of data centre capacity went from about $18 billion per gigawatt to $20-something billion, to now more than $40 billion per gigawatt, and that he expects that figure to keep rising.

Partners and Timing

DSX Pod is a reference design, not a product Nvidia will manufacture alone. Nvidia listed a global ecosystem working to deliver the factories worldwide in early 2027: Anduril, Armada, Bull, Crusoe, DayOne, Dell Technologies, Delta, Eaton, Foxconn through Ingrasys, Gigabyte, HPE, Lenovo, Pegatron, Quanta Cloud Technology, Schneider Electric, Vertiv and Wistron.

Operators can add capacity by adding another pod rather than redesigning a hall. For providers that lack deep in-house integration teams, a validated container lowers execution risk, though it does not lower the cost of the hardware inside it.

What to Watch Next

The first deliveries in early 2027 will test whether the 14-day claim holds at customer sites and whether partners can build the containers at scale. Pricing and power density were not disclosed and will determine whether DSX Pod becomes a standard expansion route or a premium option.
